sources.title: AS 2401: Consideration of Fraud in a Financial Statement Audit
sources.verification: Primary source opened or institutional primary record checked
sources.supported_claim: Paragraphs .05, .11, .57-.62 distinguish potential concerns from legal findings and address journal entries, adjustments and management override.
sources.limitations: Supports journal-review scope and cautious language; does not certify this software or establish universal rules.

sources.title: ISA 240 (Revised)
sources.verification: Primary source opened or institutional primary record checked
sources.supported_claim: The revised standard strengthens fraud-related auditor responsibilities and applies to financial statement periods beginning on or after 2026-12-15.
sources.limitations: Verify local adoption and applicable period with a qualified reviewer; the blueprint is not a compliance opinion.

sources.title: AS 2410: Related Parties
sources.verification: Primary source opened or institutional primary record checked
sources.supported_claim: The standard addresses identifying and assessing related-party relationships and transactions and responding to related risks.
sources.limitations: Motivates explicit entity relationships and evidence gaps; shared identifiers alone do not prove a related party.

sources.title: Key Findings from Occupational Fraud 2026: A Report to the Nations
sources.verification: Primary source opened or institutional primary record checked
sources.supported_claim: The study covers 2,402 investigated occupational-fraud cases across 143 countries/territories. Financial statement fraud appears in 6% of cases and has a $1 million median loss within that category.
sources.limitations: Selected investigated cases are not a representative prevalence estimate, product TAM, or projected savings.

sources.publisher: Gronewald et al. / Data in Brief
sources.title: Generating synthetic journal entries for audit analytics: Method and dataset
sources.verification: Primary source opened or institutional primary record checked
sources.supported_claim: The paper describes a labeled synthetic general ledger covering two fiscal years of a fictional business, using double-entry postings and injected problematic entries; it links a Zenodo dataset.
sources.limitations: An external benchmark candidate only; no dataset was downloaded or redistributed. Original record and license must be verified before use.

sources.title: Publication record: Generating Synthetic Journal Entries for Audit Analytics
sources.verification: Primary source opened or institutional primary record checked
sources.supported_claim: The authors institutional record identifies the work as Data in Brief volume 69 (2026) and describes synthetic patterns and probabilistic generation.
sources.limitations: Corroborates provenance; not independent validation of real-world generalization.

sources.title: Anomaly Detection in General Ledger Data: Results from a Hybrid Approach
sources.publication_date_note: 2026-09-16 arXiv submission; page says presented at a 2024 conference
sources.verification: Primary source opened or institutional primary record checked
sources.supported_claim: The research-in-progress paper studies combining journal entry tests with machine learning on synthetic normal and anomalous entries.
sources.limitations: Direct related work; hybrid rules plus models is not a novelty claim for this project.

sources.title: Detection of Anomalies in Large Scale Accounting Data using Deep Autoencoder Networks
sources.verification: Primary source opened or institutional primary record checked
sources.supported_claim: The paper proposes an autoencoder-based anomaly assessment for journal entries and reports experiments on two real accounting datasets.
sources.limitations: Alternative method for literature comparison; this handoff does not claim access to those datasets or reuse their performance.

sources.title: Leakage and the Reproducibility Crisis in ML-based Science
sources.verification: Primary source opened or institutional primary record checked
sources.supported_claim: The paper documents data leakage as a source of unreproducible machine-learning scientific findings.
sources.limitations: Motivates auditable split and feature-availability tests; the specific split protocol here is a project design.

sources.title: Common pitfalls and recommended practices
sources.verification: Primary source opened or institutional primary record checked
sources.supported_claim: The documentation describes data leakage and recommends fitting preprocessing only on training subsets, with pipelines helping enforce boundaries.
sources.limitations: Pin application library versions when implementing; current documentation is not a tested dependency lockfile.

sources.title: IsolationForest
sources.verification: Primary source opened or institutional primary record checked
sources.supported_claim: The estimator offers unsupervised anomaly scoring; its score direction and offset need to be interpreted consistently.
sources.limitations: Candidate algorithm, not a calibrated fraud probability. Freeze score orientation and preprocessing in tests.

sources.title: Metrics and scoring
sources.verification: Primary source opened or institutional primary record checked
sources.supported_claim: The documentation defines ranking/classification measures including precision-recall and average precision.
sources.limitations: Use exact named metric definitions; review-budget recall, coverage and case deduplication require project-specific definitions.
